newsitem.title: UK: UK, Dutch to join forces on military helicopters.
newsitem.headline: UK, Dutch to join forces on military helicopters.

text.p: Britain and the Netherlands have agreed to cooperate in the support and operation of their Apache and transport helicopters, the UK Ministry of Defence said in a statement on Thursday.
The Dutch are buying the McDonnell Douglas AH-64D Apache direct from the United States; the UK is buying a variant from GKN-Westland Helicopters in western England.
Both countries also operate the Boeing Chinook transport helicopter.
There is also some commonality between the RAF's Puma and the Cougar currently being acquired by the Dutch.
The ministry said the two countries have signed a Memorandum of Understanding on the cooperation plan.
"By ensuring that UK and Netherlands aircraft retain maximum commonality, both the through-life costs and the cost of logistic support will be minimised," its statement said.
James Arbuthnot, UK Minister for Defence Procurement, welcomed the agreement, saying, "It is increasingly important to look for ways of reducing the costs of supporting defence."
"Cooperation not only provides the scope for achieving this, but it also brings the additional benefits of greater inter-operability and closer operational ties," he added.
